learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will learn how to change words from one (singular) to many (plural) using regular rules and memorizing irregular ones.]
warm_up_hook: ✨ Magic trick time! How do you turn one cat into many cats? Just add an 's'! But wait, not all words are that easy. Let's learn the secret spell to turn any single thing into many!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Singular means 'only one'. Plural means 'more than one'. Most words change from singular to plural by just adding '-s' or '-es' at the end.
examples_or_templates: Add 'es' (words ending in ch, sh, s, x, o): box -> boxes, potato -> potatoes, bus -> buses

lesson_modules.teaching_content: If a noun ends in a consonant + 'y', we drop the 'y' and add '-ies'. If a noun ends in 'f' or 'fe', we drop the 'f/fe' and add '-ves'.
examples_or_templates: Rule for Y: baby -> babies, city -> cities
Rule for F/FE: leaf -> leaves, knife -> knives

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Some nouns are rebels! They do not follow the 's' or 'es' rule at all. The whole word changes. We just have to remember them like a secret code.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the plural forms: 1. Bench  2. Wolf
✍️ Fill in the blank: The cat ran after three ________ (mouse).
subjective_practice.hint: Mouse is a rebel word! It changes completely.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct this sentence: 'The baby are playing with their toy.'
subjective_practice.hint: Since 'are' and 'their' show plural, what should happen to 'baby' and 'toy'?

activity_or_assignment.title: 🃏 The Memory Match Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take 10 small paper cards. Write 5 singular words on half of them (Child, Leaf, Fox, Woman, City) and their plurals on the other half. Turn them upside down and play a memory matching game!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Singular means one; Plural means more than one.
⭐ Add '-s' or '-es' to most words to make them plural.
⭐ Drop the 'y' and add '-ies' for words like baby -> babies.
⭐ Irregular nouns change completely, like mouse -> mice and child -> children.
